$comment: THE GUARD REGISTRY — every enforcement promise Quad makes.
`scripts/guards.test.mjs` reads this file. Four rules make it more than a
1. A `live` guard names an implementation AND a literal string that
implementation contains. Rename the assertion and the registry fails,
so a guard cannot quietly stop existing.
2. A `live` guard must actually RUN — reached by `pnpm quad:gate`,
`quad:test` or `quad:typecheck`. A check nobody invokes is no check.
3. Every guard names the DECISION it protects. A guard defending nothing
recorded is one whose reason is forgotten and which is then deleted as
noise by somebody who cannot see what it was for.
4. An `owed` guard names a stage, and a SHIPPED stage may owe nothing —
which is what makes the stage table in PLAN.md mean anything.
`fails` is a consequence in the world, never a restatement of the assertion:
"a tenant's records unreachable after a move", not "the key is wrong".

guards.proves: refuses a shard whose schema does not cover the tenant's apps
guards.fails: every request for one customer answering "no such table", after a move that reported success

guards.proves: refuses a shard in the wrong place, whatever else is true of it
guards.fails: a business told their customers' records stay in the EU, and a rebalance that moved them out

guards.proves: stops accepting at the ceiling, and says nothing about who is already there
guards.fails: a number an operator typed becoming an outage trigger at whatever hour it is crossed

guards.proves: counts a disabled app when deciding what a shard needs
guards.fails: records stranded by a move, readable again the day the product is switched back on — in a database that cannot read them
a document nothing links to, drifting unread until somebody quotes it back as current
a stage marked shipped with unfinished work inside it, so "shipped" stops meaning anything
a hand-typed count wrong within a week, and a document that stops being read for the parts that are right
a guard whose reason nobody can find, deleted as noise by somebody who cannot see what it was for
a contract layer that needs a binding to test, so the rules stop being provable and start being fixtures
a shared module that knows what a client is, which has stopped being shared
`quad` meaning four different things inside the thing called Quad
consistency that is maintained by care rather than enforced, which lasts until the first hurried screen
a bottom bar that stopped being tappable and became a menu
a mechanism built, tested and wired with nowhere a person can look — every suite green
a switch somebody turns on that does nothing, so they stop watching the thing it promised
a concern an app can forget, forgotten invisibly — no error, no failing test, a capability that silently does not apply
an app writing the vault's own tables directly, so a fact exists with no grant, no consent record and no way to shred it
an operator console that gets slower with every shard, until the sweep it runs times out
cold start growing with the catalogue, until the catalogue that was meant to grow cannot
a wrong payload becoming a production error where it had been a compile error
a declaration that has to be executed before it can be read, so every generated surface stops being derivable
one of our own rules living inside somebody else's package, re-learned from their release notes
a message switched on in the policy screen that never arrives, so people stop trusting the ones that do
somebody turning on a control that does nothing, and no longer watching for the problem it promised to solve
money taken for a capability every customer already has, failing in the generous direction so nobody reports it
somebody's health record in a product table, outside consent, outside the grant log and outside crypto-shredding
a deletion request that reports success and leaves the rows, because the sweep had nothing to follow

guards.proves: refuses a statement that would fail quietly
guards.fails: a DROP running itself on every shard at 3am because somebody edited a declaration
a generated schema built from something a request supplied, which is the injection this whole design forecloses
a manifest that can call the machinery, which is a manifest that can leave a gate out of the next handler
a customer answering on the hostname a certificate authority validates against, or on the operator's own door
a handler that runs for somebody who was never allowed to call it, because one call site forgot the check

guards.proves: answers a replay with the first answer
guards.fails: a phone that retried in a basement getting a second charge, a second notification and two of what it made once

guards.proves: records an attempt that was refused
guards.fails: an incident review asking who tried and finding silence, because only the successes were recorded
a two-step escalation: invite a second address of your own as an owner, then sign in as it

guards.proves: they claim it by signing in as it
guards.fails: anybody holding an account id adding themselves to a workspace they were never invited to

guards.proves: resolved from the roster on every request
guards.fails: a role taken away that keeps working until the person signs out, which is exactly when it matters that it does not

guards.proves: cannot be started from inside somebody else's workspace
guards.fails: somebody who followed a colleague's link being invited to start a second workspace on that workspace's own branded page
a six-digit password with unlimited attempts, and a sign-in endpoint anybody can use to mail somebody a hundred times
